turns.content: For 0<t1<...<tm<1, let t0=0 and t_{m+1}=1. Prove that some interval (t_{i-1},t_{i+1}) isolates t_i and has length at least 1/(floor(m/2)+1), interpreted by a limiting argument when equality is approached.
Assume all 4n x-projections are distinct, apply the one-dimensional lemma directly to them, and extend the interval through the full square height.

Assume the sufficient condition obtained in the preceding fiber argument fails throughout. Aggregate the resulting inequalities to prove the strict boundary a>2/(N+4) for this contrary case; treat the single-group case separately if needed.
Specialize N=4n to show that every configuration has a singleton axis-parallel rectangle of area at least 1/(2n+2).

For a clustered configuration matching the size parameter established above, place each cluster near (i/(n+1),1/2) with horizontal and vertical offsets +/-epsilon, and bound every singleton rectangle as epsilon tends to zero.
Combine the lower bound and clustered construction to determine the sharp value of mu.
Determine whether this sharp guaranteed area increases or decreases with n.
Check that both bounds use open axis-parallel rectangles contained in the open unit square and verify the monotonicity algebraically.
Report the sharp value and its direction of change with n.
